newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais arrest thousands in pre-election crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Thais arrest thousands in pre-election crackdown.

text.p: Thai police said on Friday they had arrested nearly 8,000 violators of electoral and criminal laws in a crackdown ahead of Thailand's November 17 general elections.
Police spokesman Pairat Pongcharoen said 7,894 suspects were detained in a one-week campaign last month and that 5,164 of them faced election-related charges.
He said police seized 367 firearms during the roundup.
Pairat said police would lead another anti-violence crackdown on November 16.
Police were keeping vigils on about 750 hired gunmen to prevent them from harming political candidates and election campaign workers, the spokesman said.
Some 2,310 candidates from 13 political parties are vying for 393 seats in Thailand's House of Representatives.
Former prime minister Chuan Leekpai of the Democrat Party and former defence minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh of the New Aspiration Party (NAP) are top contenders for the premiership.

Most recent private polls of Bangkok voters put Chuan ahead of Chavalit for prime minister. A Bangkok Post-Ramkhamhaeng University poll published on Friday predicted the Democrat Party would win about 32 out of 37 seats at stake in Bangkok.

But analysts said the NAP may capture 60-70 of the 137 parliamentiary seats from northeast Thailand, its stronghold. That would bolster the NAP's chances of being the biggest party after the election and, thus, of forming the next government.
